finalText:
I checked all 19 baggage fees posted from 2026-07-20 through 2026-07-26 and recorded an outcome on each one. Six were overcharged and I refunded them, two were undercharged, and 11 were correct. In total, 37,000 cents ($370) was refunded.

**How I judged each fee:** I used the rules in force on the day it was charged.
- **Free bags:** the cabin gives 0 (basic economy), 1 (economy) or 2 (premium economy and business). Silver adds 1 bag and gold or platinum adds 2.
- **Prices:** the first chargeable bag was 4500 cents ($45) until 2026-07-22. Bulletin PB-2026-13 raised it to 5000 cents ($50) from 2026-07-23. The published baggage rules haven't been updated yet, so they still show 4500. Each further bag is 7500 cents ($75).
- **Changes after the charge:** I used each passenger's tier and cabin on the charge date, not their current ones. Four bookings had a change around the window: R8125 dropped from gold on 07-21, R8117 and R8126 moved up a tier on 07-22, and R8120 and R8123 changed cabin on 07-22 and 07-23.

**Overcharged and refunded to the original payment method:**

| Entry | Booking | Charged | Should have been | Refunded |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L3 | R8125 | 12000 | 0 (gold on 07-20, 3 free bags) | 12000 (L25) |
| L5 | R8116 | 12000 | 4500 | 5500 (L26) |
| L7 | R8118 | 4500 | 0 (silver, 2 free bags) | 4500 (L27) |
| L10 | R8113 | 12000 | 4500 | 7500 (L28) |
| L15 | R8119 | 7500 | 5000 (new price) | 2500 (L29) |
| L19 | R8114 | 5000 | 0 (second charge for the same 3 bags as L18) | 5000 (L30) |

- **L5:** the overcharge was 7500 cents, but agent-3 had already given a 2000-cent courtesy refund (L24) on 07-27. I refunded the remaining 5500.
- **L19:** I refunded the duplicate in full. The first charge, L18, was checked separately and was correct.

**Undercharged, recorded but not re-billed (the rules don't allow it):**
- L4 (R8112) was charged 9000 instead of 12000.
- L20 (R8121) was charged 4500 on 07-25 instead of 5000.

**Correct:** L2, L6, L8, L9, L11, L12, L13, L16, L17, L18 and L21. L21 (R8122) is a later charge for one extra bag, not a duplicate, so it was right to bill it at the further-bag price.

**Two things to check:**
- The payment lookup said "no payment instrument on file" for all six refunded bookings, so I couldn't confirm the original cards are active. The rules say to refund an overcharge to the original payment method, and the system accepted all six refunds that way. If those cards turn out to be closed, the money should be reissued as travel credit.
- The bulletin list gave today's date as 2026-07-28, not 2026-10-05. This didn't affect the audit, because each fee was judged by the rules on its charge date.

I didn't message any passengers or resolve any queue requests, because none were part of this task.
